outcome: Keep every account scored and tiered against your written ICP by a deployed agent that re-scores as accounts arrive and as the ICP changes, writing the rationale back to the CRM.

variations.when: You need fixed cost and exact reproducibility, or an LLM judgement is not acceptable to your team
variations.trade: The criteria move out of the ICP markdown and into code, so they stop being reviewable by non-engineers, and you lose the rationale entirely

variations.when: You want the score on the model directly and do not need it visible in the CRM
variations.trade: Reps lose the score and rationale where they actually work. The native's input is untyped, so confirm the field shape on the first run

variations.when: You have no CRM, or you do not want to hand this skill a CRM credential
variations.trade: Every other CRM-dependent skill you install later brings a CRM connector of its own; reuse one

outcome: Keep CRM accounts filled and refresh them when they go stale: a deployed play that fills approved blank firmographics from LinkedIn and re-enrolls a record after six months.

variations.when: The consumer uses Salesforce or Attio instead of HubSpot
variations.trade: Live generated types must be rechecked; a guessed flag writes or no-ops silently

variations.when: The approved contract differs from the starting recommendation
variations.trade: Each added field expands mapping, type-review, and the "already filled" filter

variations.when: Only a governed subset should be enriched
variations.trade: Narrower scope reduces coverage and paid calls

variations.when: Populated fields must be refreshed after explicit approval
variations.trade: Refresh can overwrite CRM-authoritative values if the preview and the write disagree

outcome: Stand up your account universe as a deployed pipeline: a Sales Navigator company search split past the 1,000 extraction cap, resolved to real domains, deduped into a shared accounts model.

variations.when: You do not want to source from LinkedIn at all, or Sales Nav does not cover your market
variations.trade: You lose the Sales Nav facet taxonomy that makes the split tactic mechanical, and the splitting has to be redesigned around the new source's own limits

variations.when: You want to see and filter the raw market before paying to enrich it
variations.trade: Nothing reaches `accounts`, so no downstream skill (scoring, contact sourcing, signals) has anything to work with until you promote

variations.when: The market search is large and you want to see the cost curve before committing
variations.trade: Your TAM is deliberately incomplete until you widen it, so do not score or report on coverage from a sample
